description: Crack Bear's 3-digit vault! Build numbers with hundreds flats, tens rods and ones cubes, meet the Zero Hero, swap digits and ride the skip-count elevator.

youtube.title: Hundreds Tower! Place Value to 999 | Hundreds, Tens and Ones | Grade 2 Math | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
Bear's vault has a 3-digit lock. To crack it, we learn place value: 10 ones make a ten, 10 tens make a hundred.
Build 345 and write it in expanded form, meet the Zero Hero (305 is not 35), swap the digits 4, 7 and 2 into six numbers, skip count by 5s, 10s and 100s, and compare numbers with greater than and less than.
Try at home: make a place value mat and build your house number.

do.text: Hundreds Tower
I built this vault. It has a three-digit lock!
A note! The code is a 3-digit number. Build it to open me.
Easy! One, two, three!
We need clues. And we need to know what each digit means.
Here are our building blocks. A little cube is one.
Let's stack ten ones.
10 ones make 1 ten. A ten is a rod.
Same amount, just one piece. Clever.
Ten ones, one ten. Say it with me! Ten ones, one ten!
Building with tens is much faster than with ones.
Now let's line up ten rods.
When I say ten tens make, you say one hundred!
Ten tens make...?
One hundred! A hundred is a flat.
A flat has 100 little squares: 10 rows of 10.
Count the rows by tens: 10, 20, 30... all the way to 100!
Fun fact: Ancient Egyptians wrote 100 as a coiled rope!
And their sign for 1,000 was a lotus flower.
But why do we need flats at all?
A flat is quicker than counting 100 cubes, one by one!
Let's build 345. Bear, please bring 3 hundreds.
One hundred, two hundred, three hundred!
Now 4 tens.
And 5 ones.
Let's check. How many hundreds?
3 hundreds! How many tens?
4 tens! And how many ones?
5 ones!
Let's read it. 3 hundreds, 4 tens, 5 ones.
Three hundred forty-five!
We can also write it in expanded form.
expanded form
300 plus 40 plus 5.
Expanded form shows what each digit is really worth.
What is the 4 worth in 345?
40! The 4 is in the tens place, so it means 4 tens.
And the 3 is worth 300,
because it sits in the hundreds place.
Make a mat at home: hundreds, tens and ones on paper.
Where a digit sits tells its worth. That's place value!
place value
Now watch. I take away all the tens.
3 hundreds, no tens, 5 ones.
Zero tens. So we write a zero in the tens place!
Thirty-five!
No, Robo! That's three hundred five.
Read it with me: three hundred five.
Oops! You're right. Three hundred five.
But why does the 0 matter if it's nothing?
The zero holds the place! Without it, we'd write 35.
And 35 is only 3 tens and 5 ones. Much smaller!
Move the zero to the end, and it's 350!
In 350, there are zero ones. The zero holds that place too.
So zero is a hero. It keeps every digit in its place.
Here's a trick. Three digit cards: 4, 7 and 2.
Same three digits. How many numbers can they make?
Six different numbers from the same three digits!
Which is the biggest?
742! The biggest digit goes in the hundreds place.
And the smallest?
247! The smallest digit goes first.
In 742, the 7 is worth 700. In 472, it's worth 70.
And in 247, it's worth just 7!
Say all six with me, smallest to biggest!
Chick, ride the skip-count elevator!
Jump on every floor! First, count by fives.
Back down! Now count by tens, starting at 120.
Now by hundreds! Jump with your arms up!
And one more than 999 is 1,000. A whole new place!
Stomp, stomp, clap! Chant with me!
Ones go here, tens go there,
hundreds stand tall in the big chair!
One hundred, two hundred, three hundred, more!
Seven hundred, eight hundred, nine hundred, more!
Ones go here, tens go there,
hundreds stand tall in the big chair!
Challenge! Let's crack Bear's vault. Clue one.
I have 5 hundreds.
My tens digit is 2.
I have 8 ones.
Clues are like a recipe for a number. Hundreds, tens, ones.
What number did we build?
528! Five hundred twenty-eight.
Bonus check clue: I am 10 more than 518.
518 plus 10 is 528. The clues agree!
Before we try the lock, a compare round.
472 or 427? Which is greater?
The hundreds are the same, 4.
So check the tens. 7 is more than 2.
472 is greater than 427.
greater than
Same hundreds. Tens: 9 is more than 0.
So 609 is less than 690!
less than
And 350 is equal to 300 plus 50.
Now type the code: 5, 2, 8!
Quiz first, then the vault! What is 600 plus 40 plus 2?
What is the 8 worth in 285?
80! The 8 is in the tens place.
Which is bigger, 309 or 390?
390! Same hundreds, and 9 tens beat 0 tens.
Count by hundreds: 200, 300, and then...?
Four out of four? You're a place value builder!
Code cracked! The vault opens!
Thank you, builders! My vault is open.
Code cracked. Place value wins.
Build your house number at home! Bye!
